title: 🗓️ Week 03 - Practical exercise
text:
Preparing Sentinel-1 Analysis Ready Data in GEE
GEE provides global-scale and analysis-ready earth observation data and the cloud computing infrastructure required for their analysis. For SAR imagery, however, Analysis Ready Data (ARD) is a concept that can vary by application.
While radiometric terrain normalization is a recommended preprocessing step for most applications, may not be conducted due to the absence of reliable DSMs. The Sentinel-1 SAR data ingested in GEE is limited to thermal noise removals, data calibration, multi-looking, and range-doppler terrain correction.
For a range of applications, it is advantageous to do additional preprocessing steps, such as speckle filtering and radiometric terrain normalization. However, expert knowledge is needed to implement the additional preprocessing steps.
Thus, in order to support additional Sentinel-1 SAR data preprocessing in GEE, Adugna Mellisa et al. (2021) proposed a comprehensive framework for preparing Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter ARD in GEE suitable for a wide range of applications.


The Mullisa workflow
The implemented framework to get Sentinel-1 ARD includes additional border noise removal, speckle filtering, and radiometric terrain normalization. All the additional preprocessing can be adjusted by the user depending on their specific needs.





Hands-on exercise
The framework is implemented in both GEE Javascript and the Python application programming interface (API).
To use the framework in GEE code editor, go to this repository and copy the contents of the s1_ard.js script to your own repository. The path to the preprocessing functions is a public so you don’t need to copy them.
When using the Python API, the user should adjust the script path and GEE id to their own path and id before processing.
Click here to try it.

title: 2027449 - PERCEPCION REMOTA AVANZADA
text:
📑 Course Brief
Focus: the focus of this course is to gain knowledge for developing novel remote sensing analysis workflows.
How: reading, learning by doing and writing


🎯 Learning Objectives

Appraise the process of image analysis and its relation to research.
Dive deep into the physical principles of multispectral remote sensing.
Distinguish the main principles of deep learning for Earth Observation data.
Apply AI techniques to obtain thematic information from Earth Observation data.



Class Atendance Policy
Students are expected to attend all classes. Occasional absences due to illness are considered excused. Participation in university activities must be requested in advance.


Artificial Intelligence Policy
Students may use generative AI to support —not replace— their own thinking, effort, and style. In any case, the use of generative AI is permitted for up to 50% of the submitted work.

DESCRIPCIÓN DE LA ASIGNATURA:






ImportantOBJETIVOS:






Conocer nuevos conceptos y técnicas de análisis de datos de percepción remota
Profundizar en tópicos avanzados de percepción remota de la superficie terrestre
Entender los conceptos básicos de deep learning aplicado a datos de observación terrestre
Aplicar métodos y técnicas de deep learning para obtener información temática a partir de imágenes ópticas y SAR


COMPETENCIAS GENÉRICAS:

Comprensión de los fundamentos teóricos de la percepción remota de la superficie terrestre
Obtención de habilidades computacionales para seleccionar, procesar y analizar imágenes
Desarrollo de pensamiento crítico sobre las ventajas y las limitaciones de diferentes técnicas



COMPETENCIAS ESPECÍFICAS:

Entendimiento del flujo de trabajo genérico de percepción remota
Adaptación y creación de scripts para procesamiento y análisis de imágenes
Entendimiento de los conceptos fundamentales de deep learning aplicado a percepción remota



METODOLOGIA:

Lectura antes de la clase a cargo del estudiante
Presentación de conceptos, métodos y técnicas a cargo del profesor
Realización de ejercicios prácticos y elaboración de reportes técnicos a cargo del estudiante



SOFTWARE

Python & Jupyter notebooks & Google Colaboratory



USO DE INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL
Los estudiantes pueden usar herramientas de Inteligencia Artifical como un apoyo, y no como un sustituto, del pensamiento, el esfuerzo y el estilo personal. En este curso se permite el uso de IA generativa hasta un máximo del 50 % de cada trabajo presentado.
